title: Your Driverless Cab Is Spying on You
key_facts: Robotaxis carry cameras inside the cabin, which companies say are needed for rider safety and to enforce rules.
In summer, Waymo staff watching in-car cameras called 911 about two teens who seemed to be firing a handgun from a Waymo in San Mateo County, California; it was an Orbeez (water bead) gun.
Waymo says its cars can automatically flag a firearm inside; earlier this year it said it used cabin cameras to check riders’ ages.
Robotaxi privacy policies are broad: footage may be used to check cleanliness and lost items, but also to improve products or services.
Zoox’s website says its interior cameras "record the entirety of your ride"; Tesla’s Robotaxi documents say riders in its early-access programme automatically opt in to data sharing.
Waymo, Zoox and Tesla say staff view interior cameras only when needed, and personal data may go to law enforcement or regulators.
Experts (Electronic Frontier Foundation, Consumer Reports) say few clear US rules govern this surveillance.
quote_evidence: Experts say that in the US, few clear rules govern this sort of surveillance, especially because riders often must agree to lengthy “terms of service” printed in minute fonts before they use ride-hailing apps.
In general, robotaxi companies including Waymo, Zoox, and Tesla say that human staff view interior cameras only when needed.
But the law hasn’t yet fully contemplated what companies should be able to see, save, and use.
why_it_matters_hint: Riders alone in a driverless car may still be recorded, and the rules on what companies do with the footage are thin.
event_date: Feature published 2 Oct 2026; examples from summer 2026, 2023 (Tesla/Reuters) and earlier this year (GM penalty)
notes: Full article read. This is a feature, not a single news event. The headline ("spying") is stronger than the article, which reports broad policies and company statements that staff look only when needed, and gives no proven misuse of robotaxi rider footage; the Tesla (2023) and GM cases concern owners’ own cars.
